feedback.problem: The graph of the function $y=f(x)$ passes through $(2,3)$ and is concave up on the interval $(0,3).$ If ${f}^{′}(2)=-1,$ estimate the value of $f(2.2)$ using the tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at $x=2$ and determine whether the approximation is an underestimate or overestimate.
feedback.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=2$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(2)+{f}^{′}(2)(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

The function passes through the point $(2,3),$ so we have $f(2)=3.$ Also, we're told that ${f}^{′}(2)=-1,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =3+(-1)(x-2) \\  & =3-(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(2.2)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=2.2.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2.2) & ≈L(2.2) \\  & =3-(2.2-2) \\  & =3-0.2 \\  & =2.8.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the function is concave up on the interval $(0,3),$ the linear approximation $L(x)$ is below the graph near $x=2,$ and therefore we have an underestimate.
